version_notes: v1.1.1 (2026-10-19): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: two kinds of reformat noise. (1) A word already in the source was flagged as a new proper noun when a reformat moved it mid-line or capitalized it (one-per-line competencies joined with " | ": Budgeting, Sales, Team). Proposed proper nouns are now compared case-insensitively against every word of the source, wherever it sits. (2) A unit letter (k, M, b) took the first letter of the next word, even across a line break ("20 Mechanics" -> "20 M"), so a rewrapped line changed the token and an old number was flagged as new; the context snippet then came from the first substring match, so "20" showed the context of "200+". Units now count only when no letter follows, and context is taken from a whole-token match. "200+" was already one token. New tools, employers and numbers still flag. Found by the owner's Mode A run (2026-10-19). v1.1.0 (2026-10-18): description only. A live trigger probe (normal tool set, user hooks off, 3 samples per prompt) showed the skill loading for 1 of 9 runs of three in-domain prompts (make me sound like I know a tool, research the company before the interview, mock panel) in both a full install and a family-only install; the base model answered directly and scripted unverified experience. The new description names company research, practice answers, mock interviews and 'sounding experienced in a skill they lack', and says to load the skill rather than answer from general knowledge. Probe with the new text: 9/9, controls 3/3. Do-not-use clauses unchanged. Owner-approved 2026-10-18. v1.0.1 (2026-10-18): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: a comma right after a number ("In 2023, four new") was kept as part of the token, so a number or year already in the source was flagged as new ("2023,", "40,"). Trailing commas are now stripped; inner commas ("1,200") are kept and truly new numbers are still flagged. Found by the first live outcome-eval run of interview-prep (2026-10-18). v1.0.0 (2026-10-18) adds interview-prep as the 8th job-hunter family member (idea borrowed from the ai-job-search /interview command, built on our own anti-fabrication rules). load_application.py reads one tracked application (tracker.json entry, the submitted resume and cover letter, posting text, confirmed LESSONS.md entries) without writing the tracker. build_prep_pack.py builds a stage-specific pack (6 stages) mapping posting requirements to the user's real lines, with STAR scaffolds, honest gap bridges, questions to ask, and source-checked research (posting URLs rejected, interviewer research kept professional). Every answer line is a blockquote; the claims subcommand extracts them for the bundled verify_no_fabrication gate (byte-identical to resume-tailor). Optional mock-interview mode. Never auto-sends or contacts anyone.
